title: CleanLASA introduction
text: CleanLASA designed make LASA (Longitudinal Aging Study Amsterdam) SPSS data easier find, import, document, prepare analysis R. package connects three parts LASA workflow otherwise require substantial manual work: finding relevant LASA topic, file code, measurement waves, variable documentation; importing LASA .sav files applying correct wave-specific variable value labels; auditing, refreshing, manually correcting metadata used labelling. central import function read_lasa_sav(). identifies LASA wave file code file name applies metadata package’s normalized label database. labelling engine available separately apply_lasa_labels() data already imported. typical workflow therefore: examples involving LASA data files live LASA website run vignette built, LASA data distributed package website access may available package installation.

title: Import and Clean LASA SPSS Data
text: read_lasa_sav() (apply_lasa_labels(), ) accepts five reshaping arguments: name_corrections – manually point canonical suffix (e.g. lphya08) differently-named source column, known typo/renaming data. to_factor – convert categorical variables factors, using SPSS value labels levels. to_numeric – restore count/continuous variables plain numeric, converting negative (missing-reason) codes NA. standardize_names – rename every matched column canonical lowercase LASA name wave code removed (e.g. lphya01), standardize "respnr" (capitalization) "respnr". Always implies split_wavecode = TRUE well. split_wavecode – move wave-letter prefix variable names (e.g. blphya01 becomes lphya01) new "LASA_wave" column, inserted right "respnr" filled file’s wave code (e.g. "B", "2B", "3B"). Regardless arguments, every matched column also keeps original SPSS value coding available reference attributes – attr(x, "original_labels") (codebook) attr(x, "original_values") (raw imported values) – R output can always cross-checked another program’s (e.g. SPSS) coding, even to_numeric/ to_factor reshaping. importing, can check whether variables matched LASA documentation using lasa_label_report(): returns set “faulty” variables — ones couldn’t matched corresponding documentation — can inspect resolve analysis.
code: # Rename columns to their canonical names and split the wave code into its # own column, all in one call: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav", standardize_names = TRUE) names(data)[1:3] #> [1] "respnr"    "LASA_wave" "lphya01"  # split_wavecode also works on its own, without fully standardizing names: data <- read_lasa_sav("LASAB046.sav", split_wavecode = TRUE) lasa_label_report(data)

text: Topic, theme, subtheme matching case-insensitive. Incomplete names small typographical errors accepted fuzzy_match = TRUE. Supplying theme searches main LASA themes subthemes. LASA topics documented several related file codes one row topic table, main file, telephone-interview version, longitudinally cleaned version. LASA site's label row spells (example "Self-report chronic diseases - tel. proxy - tel. respondent"), file code returned part label describes (e.g. "Self-report chronic diseases - tel. proxy" proxy-interview file code) rather full combined label repeated every code. Splitting prefers row's column layout falls back LASA file-code numbering convention (0/1 = main face--face file, 2/3 = processed derived file, 4/5 = longitudinally cleaned revised file, 6 = telephone interview proxy, 7 = telephone interview respondent); single file code covers several qualifiers (nothing disambiguate), full descriptive list dropped favor plain base topic name. small number rows need information present compact topic-table text - lives file code's variable-information PDF, topic page's prose, specific domain knowledge - scraper can derive table alone. rows carry curated, documented correction (see data-raw/lasa_topic_overrides.R package source full list reasoning behind one). curation applied every time table built, independently refresh.
